title: Modeling ecological drivers in marine viral communities using comparative metagenomics and network analyses
author: Bonnie Hurwitz
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.efgbbjw
materials: Log into to iPlant/CyVerse (http://www.cyverse.org/, http://de.iplantcollaborative.org) Discovery Environment.
a Optional args: K-mer size: Default is

steps.title: Prepare FASTA and metadata files
steps.instruction: Upload FASTA‑formatted sequence files and a tab‑delimited metadata file. Example data are located at "/iplant/home/shared/imicrobe/fizkin/pov"; view them in the Discovery Environment by clicking the Data button, then navigating to Community Data → imicrobe → fizkin → pov → fasta. The sample metadata file is named "meta.tab". Ensure the metadata headers include a 'name' column and fields ending in .d (discrete), .c (continuous), or .ll (latitude/longitude). Do not use underscores in field names except for "lat_long.ll".

steps.title: Open Fizkin app and set required arguments
steps.instruction: In the Discovery Environment, select the Apps button, then choose Public Apps → Experimental → iMicrobe → Fizkin. In the Required Args section, set your FASTA directory as the "Input directory" and locate your metadata file (from step 1) as the "Metadata file". You may leave the "Output directory" as default or change it.

substeps.instruction: Mode minimum: default 1; increase for more stringent matching.
Max. num. sequences: default 300 K; lower to reduce runtime, higher for deeper coverage. Samples exceeding this number are randomly sampled.
Max. num. samples: default 15; because Fizkin performs pair‑wise analysis (runtime O(n²)), samples above this limit are randomly selected.
Files list: provide a text file listing the subset of FASTA files to run, one file per line.

steps.title: Launch analysis and monitor
steps.instruction: Press "Launch analysis" and wait for the system notification indicating job completion.

steps.title: Troubleshoot metadata‑related failures
steps.instruction: If the job fails with an R error such as "Error in summary(fit1)$cov.unscaled[(2 * n):length(fit1$coef), (2 * n):length(fit1$coef)] : subscript out of bounds", the cause is usually overly homogeneous or heterogeneous metadata. Remove or correct the offending metadata columns and re‑run the analysis.

steps.title: Retrieve and interpret network graph
steps.instruction: When the job finishes successfully, the final output is a social‑network graph that visualizes grouping of samples based on similarity, similar to the example shown in the documentation.
